newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end lower, Jinro trouble continues.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end lower, Jinro trouble continues.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Thursday as the financial troubles of the Jinro Group continued, dampening sentiment, brokers said.
News that serious defects have been found in the high-speed railway now under construction also affected the market.
The composite index closed 7.66 points lower at 694.76.

Jinro said it has asked for 500 billion won in emergency loans from the Commercial Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK. "Jinro seems to have difficulties getting fresh loans despite its restructuring plans revealed on Monday," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The group said it urgently needed the money to pay back debts. Jinro Ltd 21000, the flagship liquor making unit of the group, fell 800 won to its limit of 9,600.
The group denied local reports that the sale of idle lands in Seoul to a Hong Kong company, "Jesmond Korea," was part of its restructuring plan.
A group official said Jinro sold the property for 145.6 billion won in December after dropping plans to build a hotel.
Construction shares plunged on the news that the high-speed railway has structural problems on some bridges and railway, which may need repairs.
